also: what can I do for you?

terms.gloss: how can I help you? (a shop assistant to a customer)
terms.comment: Ministrāre is classically to wait on someone, above all at table (quō commodius tibi ministrētur, Cic. Fam. 16.14.2, Lewis & Short); the shop greeting is Traupman’s. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.
Traupman’s words. Adjuvāre is as good, and the usual verb for helping someone in a task (see I’ll help you). Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.
